Headline CPI rose 0.1% month over month and 3.4% year over year, both matching expectations, with the annual rate easing from 3.5% in June.

Core CPI increased 0.2% for the month and 2.5% year over year, also matching forecasts, with the annual core rate falling from 2.6% to its lowest level since February.

Shelter costs remained firm, with both owners' equivalent rent and primary rents rising 0.3%, while medical care and airfares also increased.

On the softer side, energy prices fell 1.5% and gasoline dropped 2.9%, helping restrain headline inflation.

Overall, the report gave the Fed additional room to remain on hold in September, with the market-implied probability of a September rate hike slipping to around 39% from 44% before the release.

However, there is still another round of inflation and employment data ahead of the September FOMC meeting, leaving plenty of time for the outlook to change.
